_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: RESOLVED #165, verified by execution and by the vendor contract. No live POST to /tags.json remains anywhere in the tree; the three surviving mentions are all explanatory comments. The two other `tags:` writes (main.js:737, background.html:364) are on POST /api/v2/tickets.json, i.e. ticket CREATION, where writing the whole set is correct and nothing pre-exists to destroy. The two addTicketTag copies are byte-identical after indent normalisation, checked by extracting both function bodies and diffing. Zendesk's own docs confirm the premise the fix rests on ('Unless otherwise specified, the set tag behavior is used, which overwrites and replaces existing tags') and confirm safe_update/updated_stamp exist and belong inside the `ticket` object, which is where the fix puts them.

RESOLVED #154, verified by execution. safeFieldId was driven with the issue's own acceptance payload `1">` and returns null; also null for '', null, undefined, -1, 1.5, '1e3' and Arabic-Indic digits; ' 42 ' returns '42'. The regex is ASCII-anchored ^[0-9]+$, so there is no Unicode-digit path into the id. Critically it is applied on BOTH sides: the render side (main.js:846) and the getElementById lookup (main.js:1013), so the lookup can only ever ask for an id that was actually written. The rejected case renders a visible 'Unavailable' placeholder built from string literals, not from partner data. Category 7 re-swept around it: every innerHTML interpolation in the card, notes, partner-search and form paths is esc()-wrapped, and partner results use textContent.

RESOLVED #152, verified by execution rather than by reading the new keyword's documentation. The two markers have genuinely different privilege. With the shipped `audit-degrades: v1-webhooks ... tracked-by ...#153`, the call is reported twice (the new degrades WARN and the sunsetting WARN, which still names background.html). Swapping the same key to `audit-allow` removes background.html from the sunsetting WARN entirely and moves it to the 'deliberate' WARN. So audit-degrades cannot be used to clear an audit-allow-class finding, which was the obvious way this could have gone wrong. tracked-by is enforced and fails CLOSED: a degrades marker with no tracked-by is a FAIL naming file, line and the missing clause, both with and without an expiry.

RESOLVED #161 (noted item from the previous record, not a filed issue), verified by enumeration at 4cbca06. All 7 tsanetGet call sites in main.js and all 4 in background.html pass either (path) or (path, 'v2'); no positional boolean survives anywhere. Both files now declare tsanetGet(path, version, retried), matching main.js's own tsanetPost(path, body, retried). The transposition hazard is gone.

MEDIUM, NEW THIS ROUND, recommended as an escalation of #164 rather than a new issue: the v1-base anchor assertion added by #163 PASSES on a MISREAD default, which reopens #151's exit-0 end state in pure ES5 with zero caller changes. _baseurl_default takes the FIRST quoted /v\d+/ token in the declaration span, so it is a heuristic, not semantics; the assertion only asks 'did I read something', never 'is what I read correct'. Probed by importing the module and calling the functions directly: baseline (|| 'v1') -> default v1, on_v1_base True. Explicit-branch rewrite with || 'v1' removed -> default MISREAD as v2, on_v1_base False, and anchor FAIL False, so no finding fires. The same rewrite with || 'v1' retained is rescued by the old v1_base regex, as is a mere comment mentioning 'v2', so the hole is a conjunction: an earlier quoted v-token AND || 'v1' gone. Composed end state probed on the tree (that rewrite + drop the now-orphaned marker + migrate scripts/rotate-inbound-webhook.py to v2, which is #101's declared scope): EXIT 0, 20 PASS, 0 warn, 0 fail, anchor check PASS, and tsanetGet('/webhooks') still live at background.html:96 and still in the bundle members install. The middle step is INVITED by the suite: after the rewrite the stale-marker WARN says the marker 'excused nothing', which tells the author to delete it. Also branch-order dependent: writing the v1 branch first reads 'v1' and no hole opens, which is what confirms the defect is the first-token heuristic and means the fix must be #164's explicit `audit-anchor:` declaration, not a lint against branching.

LOW, NEW THIS ROUND: the stale-marker WARN prints the marker KIND, not the key. scripts/security-audit.py:835 still reads mk.group(1). #162 renumbered ALLOW_MARKER's groups (1=kind, 2=key, 3=date, 4=malformed, 5=tracker) and correctly updated _matches_unmarked (613), the `marked` tuple (624-625) and _excuses (642, 646), but not 835, which also hardcodes the literal prefix 'audit-allow:'. Probed: a stale `audit-allow: v1-typo-key` reports as 'audit-allow: allow'; a stale `audit-degrades: v1-typo-key` reports as 'audit-allow: degrades', which is wrong in both halves. The check exists (per its own comment) to catch 'a typo'd key or a call that moved', and the key is the one thing it can no longer name. EVERY other ALLOW_MARKER group consumer was audited and 835 is the ONLY stale one, so this cannot suppress a finding: the WARN still fires and still names file and line. Same defect class as the already-filed #160. Four check-name labels (851, 855, 863, 866) also still read 'audit-allow' now that a second keyword exists, which is how a degrades tracked-by failure comes to be reported under 'every audit-allow marker is dated and current'.

LOW, NEW THIS ROUND: the outbound submit path reports 'Submit failed' for a collaboration request that WAS created. main.js:1021 returns addTicketTag(ticketId, 'tsanet_outbound') inside the submit chain BEFORE showSuccess, so a rejection falls to the outer .catch -> showError('Submit failed: ' + ...) with the dialog left open and populated. By then tsanetPost('/collaboration-requests') has succeeded and writeFields has run: the case exists on TSANet and the partner has it. The security-relevant consequence is not the wrong message but what it induces: a re-submit opens a SECOND collaboration request to the partner organization, i.e. unintended duplicate cross-org transmission. Pre-#167 this path could only fail exceptionally (network/auth); safe_update is ENGINEERED to reject on concurrent modification, and an agent opening a collaboration request from a live support ticket is exactly when triggers, automations and other agents touch that ticket, so #167 converts a rare failure into a by-design one. One retry absorbs the ordinary race, so the residual is narrow. This interacts with the unverified 409 below in one direction only: if the collision status is NOT 409 the retry never fires and this triggers on the FIRST ordinary race rather than the residual, never the reverse. The recommended fix (treat the tag as best-effort, since it is a filterability convenience and not part of the case) is robust under either status code.

MEDIUM #153: the residual v1 probe call is still tracked by nothing other than this issue, but the marker now names it. #162's tracked-by clause points at #153 from background.html:96 and the suite FAILs if it is removed, so the marker and its tracker are no longer unlinked. The finding itself stays open until the call is deleted. OPEN, not accepted, BLOCKING.

HIGH #144: no release exists. Re-verified this round: v1.0.54 is still the newest tag and the newest GitHub Release, while the manifest at 4cbca06 reads 1.0.60. Six manifest revs (1.0.55 through 1.0.60) are in main and in no installable artifact. Members today run v1.0.54, which carries the destructive tag write #165 documents, the fail-open probe #148 removed and the unguarded 401 retry #155 removed. Nothing in this delta argues against cutting the release; the delta strictly improves the shipped bundle, and this is the largest such gap yet recorded. OPEN, not accepted, BLOCKING.

LOW #164: the v1-base anchor is inferred from a JS declaration. OPEN. Recommended for escalation to medium-priority this round, with the ES5 probe above as evidence, because #164's recorded low rationale ('Moving baseUrl onto an object changes every caller, so it is a deliberate restructure rather than a tidy-up... None of this is reachable without an ES6 rewrite the codebase shows no sign of') is falsified for the new member: it needs no ES6 and changes zero callers. Bundle measured this round at main.js 167 var / 0 const / 0 let / 0 arrow / 0 ??; background.html 26/0/0/0/0.
LOW #160: the PASS line that reads 'no known-deprecated endpoint usage found' while a marked v1 call is in the tree. OPEN, unchanged by this delta.
LOW #156: sanitizeHtml's allowlist consults the prototype chain. Untouched by this delta and NOT re-cleared.

LOW #157: stripHtml decodes entities after stripping tags. Untouched by this delta and NOT re-cleared. Noted, not a finding: every stripHtml call site in the notes path wraps its output in esc(), so the re-introduced markup is escaped again before it reaches innerHTML.

MEDIUM #166 (bug label, not security): the SLA breach poller is not direction-scoped. OPEN and untouched by #167. Noted here only because #167 REDUCES its blast radius: a false-positive outbound breach now adds a wrong tag instead of also wiping the ticket's entire tag set.
MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly. OPEN, accepted by Shawn 2026-07-28.
MEDIUM #96: durable audit trail. OPEN, accepted.
MEDIUM #119: move the ZAF app off the TSANet API user password to the ZIS Entra client credential. OPEN, accepted.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131. OPEN, accepted.
notes: Extends the record from 9cbcc87 to 4cbca06 (manifest 1.0.57 -> 1.0.60; none of 1.0.55 through 1.0.60 is in any release). The delta is five commits, one of which is the previous record. The four source PRs are #161 (tsanetGet signature), #162 (audit-degrades keyword + safeFieldId), #163 (v1-base anchor assertion) and #167 (addTicketTag union write). Files touched: scripts/security-audit.py, zaf-build/assets/background.html, zaf-build/assets/main.js, zaf-build/manifest.json. .github/ and zis/ untouched, confirmed by `git diff --name-only 9cbcc87..origin/main -- .github/ zis/` returning empty.

THREE CLAIMED CLOSURES VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING THE DIFF: #154 by driving safeFieldId with the issue's own acceptance payload and eleven edge cases; #152 by swapping the shipped marker's keyword and observing that audit-degrades does not remove the call from the sunsetting WARN while audit-allow does; #165 by grepping the tree for surviving tags.json writes, diffing the two addTicketTag bodies, and confirming the vendor contract for both the replace behaviour and safe_update. #161 verified by enumerating every call site rather than trusting the commit message's claim to have done so.

SELF_REVIEWED IS FALSE, WITH A CAVEAT I CANNOT RESOLVE FROM THIS SESSION. This reviewer did not write any of the four PRs. However #164, which this review builds on and recommends escalating, is recorded as coming from a QA re-review of #163, and I cannot establish from this session whether that was the same agent. Treat the independence claim as unverified rather than asserted. The standing request for a second signer carries.

THE MECHANICAL SUITE WAS RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY at 4cbca06: 18 PASS, 2 WARN, 0 FAIL, exit 2, matching the numbers supplied with the request. The two WARNs are the new degrades WARN naming background.html:96 and the sunsetting WARN naming rotate-inbound-webhook.py and background.html. Beyond running it, check_deprecated_endpoints was probed BY MUTATION on seven variants (marker keyword swap, tracked-by present/absent, expiry present/absent, four baseUrl spellings) and the anchor functions were exercised by importing the module directly. The suite's other checks (SRI, pinning, permissions, expression injection, embedded secrets, secure settings) were NOT re-probed by mutation this round; their correctness rests on reading plus their PASS output.

CATEGORIES WITH NO DELTA, stated as no-delta rather than as clean. Category 1: no change; .github/ untouched, and the manifest diff across the whole delta is the version string ONLY (1.0.57 -> 1.0.60), verified by diffing the file. Categories 3, 4, 5: the delta adds no endpoint, no destination, no field, no permission and no log statement. domainWhitelist is still exactly the two connect2 hosts; tsanet_password is still the only secure parameter. addTicketTag adds a GET and a PUT against a ticket the app could already write, using the same ZAF session, so it widens no authorization surface. Category 7 WAS re-reviewed this round because #162 lands in it, and the sinks are re-inventoried above; #156 and #157 remain open and nothing here re-clears them. Categories 2 and 6 are where the marker and anchor work lives and are covered above.

GATE CONSEQUENCE OF ADVANCING TO 4cbca06. COVERED becomes true: the mechanical suite exits 2, which release.yml classifies as 'warnings only' and not a coverage flag; the record parses; 4cbca06 is an ancestor of any tag cut from main; and `git diff --name-only 4cbca06..HEAD -- zaf-build/ zis/ scripts/ .github/workflows/` is empty, so committing this record does not itself create drift, because .security-audit.json sits outside the watched set. THE BLOCKING SET SHRANK THIS ROUND, for the first time: #152, #154 and #158 all closed, leaving #144 (high) and #153 (medium) as the only issues that are security-labelled, not low-priority and not accepted. Read out of release.yml's own classifier this round rather than carried: low-priority issues `continue` and never block, so #164, #160, #157, #156 and #98 are reported and do not flag; #96, #119 and #140 are on accepted_issues and do not block. Cutting the release therefore requires accepting TWO issues explicitly, down from five, and #144 still cannot close until the release it blocks exists. If Shawn approves raising #164 to medium-priority, the blocking set becomes three; that is a deliberate consequence of the escalation, not a side effect.

NOTHING WAS ACCEPTED BY THIS REVIEW, no issue was filed, no severity was changed, no tag was cut and no release was made. The #164 escalation and the two new LOW findings are recommendations awaiting Shawn's go.

NOT VERIFIED, carried and updated. NEW this round: the status code a safe_update collision actually returns. Zendesk documents the parameters ('protects against ticket update collisions and returns a message to let you know if one occurs') but does NOT document the code, and the new code keys its retry on err.status === 409; not probed live. The ZAF client.request rejection shape is also undocumented on both the ZAF Client API page and the 'Making API requests from a Zendesk app' page, but there is strong LOCAL precedent (main.js:142 and background.html:171 already read err.status and err.responseJSON off ZAF rejections in pre-existing code), and if err.status were absent the retry simply never fires, which is the fail-safe direction: the write is rejected, nothing is clobbered. Also new: addTicketTag guards `d && d.ticket && d.ticket.tags` for the tag read and then dereferences d.ticket.updated_at unguarded two lines later, so a malformed GET response would throw rather than degrade; noted as a robustness inconsistency, not a finding. CARRIED: whether TSANet storage permits a non-integer fieldId to reach a client (severity of the now-closed #154 rested on the undocumented reliance, not a proven exploit); what status GET /v1/webhooks returns after removal; release.yml's behaviour under a FAILING audit, read again this round and still never exercised, reachable 2026-10-03; #138's fix, verified by inspection and by the mechanical check, not by pushing a hostile tag; PROD runtime, PROD credentials known-dead; whether GuardCreate (#41) absorbs the duplicate condition the v1.0.54 fail-open path creates today; the docx, ZIS Quick Start and GitBook surfaces. No live BETA or Zendesk probe was run this round, because the delta touches no TSANet endpoint.

SCHEDULED TIGHTENING, carried. From 2026-10-03 check_deprecated_endpoints returns FAIL for the background.html call and the coverage gate flags. The marker route cannot defer it: probed previously at the 90-day boundary, and the audit-degrades marker added by #162 never excused anything to begin with. The caveat still holds for the anchor route described in the new MEDIUM above, which is precisely why that finding is medium rather than low.

ACCEPTANCE, 2026-07-29, Shawn, for this record only. accepted_issues gains #144, #153 and #164; #96, #98, #119 and #140 carry forward. This review accepted nothing, which is the separation the persona depends on: it may tighten a gate and never loosen one, so a finding it raised or left open can only be accepted by a human. Rationale per issue. #144 is HIGH and its substance IS this release: the four sunset call sites are migrated, and the issue cannot close until the release it blocks exists, so it closes on publish rather than being carried. #153 is the residual v1 /webhooks probe, which is deliberately marked audit-degrades, reported as a WARN on every run, and owned by #101's member-subscription migration; deleting it early makes every unmigrated member read as push-not-registered. #164 is a gap in this suite's own anchor assertion and reaches nothing in the shipped bundle, and it was left at low-priority this round rather than escalated. Verified against release.yml's own classifier rather than assumed: with these three accepted, zero open security issues block, so the release publishes with no security note. #156, #157, #160, #168 and #169 are low-priority and reported only. Acceptance expires with this record — source drift invalidates coverage, so the next review re-accepts explicitly rather than inheriting this list.
